title: Automated Identity Governance for Global Retail
business: A multinational retail chain managing thousands of seasonal employees across disparate regional offices.
problem: Manual user account provisioning and deprovisioning lead to security vulnerabilities and orphaned accounts when staff turnover occurs.
solution: Utilize Windows Server Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) to centralize identity management, leveraging Group Policy Objects (GPOs) and PowerShell automation to enforce consistent access controls and automated lifecycle management.
steps: Deploy Windows Server instances configured with the Active Directory Domain Services role.
Define Organizational Units (OUs) based on regional retail locations to segment user objects.
Create PowerShell scripts to automate the creation of user accounts based on HR database exports.
Apply GPOs to restrict local administrative privileges on retail point-of-sale terminals.
Configure scheduled tasks on the domain controller to disable inactive accounts after a defined period.
outcome: A unified identity framework that ensures consistent security posture and reduces the administrative burden of manual account lifecycle management.
limitation: The primary limitation is the dependency on domain controller availability; if the primary domain controller is unreachable, authentication requests fail. Administrators can check this status using the dcdiag command to verify domain controller health and replication consistency.

questions.question: In Automated Identity Governance for Global Retail, what is the primary driver for implementing AD DS?

To increase the processing speed of point-of-sale transactions
To replace the need for HR database exports entirely
To provide cloud-native storage for retail inventory data

Dependency on domain controller availability for authentication
PowerShell scripts are incompatible with Windows Server
GPOs cannot be applied to regional retail locations
